candidates.story: Cloudflare Disallow AI Training for mixed-use crawlers and September migration
candidates.reason: The primary post supplies an exact 13:00 UTC publication time inside the priority window and documents a live product-control change and migration. Apple, Google, Microsoft and RFC records independently bound the crawler/use claims. Existing terms.txt coverage discussed the July plan, not this September shipped choice.

candidates.story: SkillAtlas attack trace library for agent skills
candidates.reason: The cs.CR RSS announced it as new at 04:00 UTC on 15 September, though v1 was submitted on 11 September. A curated red-team corpus and guarded benchmark are useful research but do not show deployed risk reduction. Cloudflare gives site operators a fresher, more direct policy decision with independent crawler documentation.

candidates.story: terms.txt machine-access proposal and July Cloudflare crawler plan
candidates.reason: Index Us published the proposal in run 20260912T140303Z. That article cites the July Cloudflare plan as context; it does not cover the separate 15 September Cloudflare release or its migration. No correction to the terms.txt research was established in this drafting pass.

decision.reason: Cloudflare published an exact-timestamped, non-duplicate mixed-use crawler setting and migration on 15 September. The article explains the actual site-operator choice between a no-training use preference with search access and access blocking that affects search, while preserving Bing and AI-summary limits.

sources.title: About Applebot

sources.title: Google common crawlers — Google-Extended
sources.locator: Google-Extended entry: no separate HTTP user agent, robots product token, affected Gemini training and named grounding uses, no Google Search inclusion/ranking effect; page says last updated 2026-07-14 UTC. Google describes its own crawler.

sources.title: Announcing new options for webmasters to control usage of their content in Bing Chat
sources.locator: September 2023 official account of NOARCHIVE exclusion from Bing Chat answers and generative-model training while ordinary Bing search indexing can remain; historical official documentation. Cloudflare s1 supplies the current claim that Bing no-training robots support is not yet available.

sources.title: RFC 9309: Robots Exclusion Protocol
sources.locator: Sections 1 and 3: robots rules are crawler access preferences, not access authorisation, and not an application-security substitute. Independent technical standard, not evaluation of Cloudflare implementation.

claims.text: Cloudflare published the mixed-use crawler setting announcement at 13:00 UTC on 15 September 2026.
Cloudflare says Disallow AI Training publishes applicable no-training preferences through Bot Preference Sync while designated mixed-use crawlers can continue ordinary search crawling.
claims.sourceLocator: s1 New security setting options; s3 Disallow paragraph

claims.text: Cloudflare says Training Block and Block on pages with ads now apply to Applebot, Bingbot and Googlebot and can therefore affect search access.
Cloudflare says Disallow AI Training blocks other training crawlers, including training-only crawlers from Amazon, Anthropic, Meta and OpenAI.
Cloudflare did not add a Disallow setting for Agent traffic in this release.
Cloudflare maps earlier granular Training Block and ads-only Block choices to Disallow AI Training to preserve their previous practical effect; legacy Block AI Bots settings have a separate mapping.
claims.sourceLocator: s1 two migration tables and explanatory paragraphs

claims.text: Cloudflare recommends Search Allow for both new-domain presets while Training and Agent presets vary with advertising monetisation.
claims.sourceLocator: s1 Recommendations for new domains table

claims.text: Cloudflare’s Bot Management update API documents ai_training set to disallow and bot_preference_sync_enabled.
claims.sourceLocator: s4 update request schema and example

claims.text: Apple says Applebot-Extended controls training use of Applebot-crawled pages, makes no separate page crawl and does not affect Apple Search rankings.
claims.sourceLocator: s5 Applebot-Extended and About search rankings

claims.text: Apple describes nosnippet and paywall markup as separate page-level controls on generated outputs.
claims.sourceLocator: s5 Customizing indexing rules and Marking paywalled content

claims.text: Google says Google-Extended is a robots product token without its own HTTP user agent and governs future Gemini training plus grounding in named Gemini products, without affecting Google Search inclusion or ranking.
Cloudflare says its Disallow AI Training setting does not yet convey a Bing no-training preference via robots.txt and that Microsoft is targeting early 2027 support.
Microsoft’s older NOARCHIVE account says tagged content can remain in ordinary Bing search while being excluded from Bing Chat answers and generative-model training.
claims.sourceLocator: s7 NOARCHIVE section; older publication requires current-use caveat

claims.text: RFC 9309 says robots.txt crawler-access rules are not access authorisation.
A published use preference cannot by itself prove downstream training compliance; a site operator should separately verify its edge access policy, crawler controls and current account migration.
claims.sourceLocator: s1 preference versus Block and migration; s3 robots publishing; s8 authorisation boundary. Practical inference, not measured efficacy
